# dtcloud_routers (Data Source)

Lists every router visible to the caller.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "dtcloud_routers" "all" {}

data "dtcloud_routers" "edge" {
  name = "edge"
}

# enable_snat also reads false on a router with no gateway at all, so is_external
# is what tells the two apart.
output "routers_without_a_gateway" {
  value = [for r in data.dtcloud_routers.all.routers : r.name if !r.is_external]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `name` (String) Only return routers with this exact name. Applied by the provider.
- `status` (String) Only return routers in this status, e.g. `ACTIVE`. Applied by the provider.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `routers` (List of Object) The routers that matched, in the order the platform returned them. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routers))

<a id="nestedatt--routers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routers`

Read-Only:

- `cidr` (String)
- `enable_snat` (Boolean)
- `external_network` (String)
- `id` (String)
- `is_external` (Boolean)
- `name` (String)
- `status` (String)

## Behaviour worth knowing

* **Both filters are applied by the provider**, after the full list has been fetched, because the
  endpoint takes no query parameters.
* **`enable_snat` reads `false` for a router with no gateway at all**, so on its own it does not
  tell "SNAT off" from "no gateway". `is_external` does.
* **The external network is a name here and an id on `dtcloud_router`.** This endpoint is not given
  the id. If you need it -- to build a matching `dtcloud_router`, for instance -- look the router up
  by id with `dtcloud_router`, or look the name up in `dtcloud_networks`.
